basic_information.official_title: AN ACT GRANTING GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES OF THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO A SPECIAL LEAVE TO PERFORM PILGRIMAGE
basic_information.approved_by: Not shown. The approval block of the published copy reads “XXX”.
basic_information.origin_bills: Parliament Bill No. 282, reported with Bill No. 276 under Committee Report No. 176
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or in a newspaper of regional circulation within the BARMM

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Gives BARMM government officials and employees with 3 years of aggregate service a paid Pilgrimage Leave of at most 22 working days, once in a lifetime, to visit a place of religious or spiritual importance.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: Section 2 frames it as workforce policy: a strong and highly motivated workforce is needed for a progressive Bangsamoro, and paid leave for pilgrimage supports spiritual and personal development, employee well-being and long-term productivity.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Eligible employees can apply once for up to 22 working days of paid leave. Approval sits with the employee's own head — minister, Speaker, governor or local chief executive — with the Chief Minister approving for heads of ministries, offices and agencies and for governors and city mayors. Afterwards the employee files a written report within 30 days, and one who deliberately does not perform the pilgrimage faces administrative sanctions.
who_will_be_affected: Officials and employees of Bangsamoro ministries, offices and agencies
Members and personnel of the Bangsamoro Parliament
Officials and employees of local government units in the BARMM, barangays included
Heads of office, who approve applications and may deny them
The Office of the Chief Minister, which keeps the region-wide record
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: 15 days after publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or a newspaper of regional circulation. Passed 16 July 2026; the published copy shows no Chief Minister approval date. Implementing rules are due within 60 days of approval.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: PASSED 16 JULY 2026. If you have served the Bangsamoro Government or a BARMM LGU for an aggregate of 3 years, you may take up to 22 working days of paid leave to perform a pilgrimage — once in your lifetime.
in_practice: At most 22 working days, paid, once in a lifetime
Requires an aggregate of 3 years of service in Bangsamoro ministries, offices, agencies or LGUs
Pilgrimage means visiting a place of religious or spiritual importance in your faith — and may include other meaningful spiritual or moral journeys recognised by your traditions or conscience
Your own head of office approves; heads of ministries, offices and agencies are approved by the Chief Minister
Approvals are copied to the Office of the Chief Minister within 10 days
A head of office may deny an application that would seriously hamper operations; a refiled application the next year gets priority
A written report on the pilgrimage is due within 30 days of returning to work
Deliberately not performing the pilgrimage after taking the leave draws administrative sanctions under Civil Service Commission rules
Unused leave cannot be converted to cash
Existing leave benefits are not reduced

for_specific_groups.Employees of Bangsamoro ministries, offi: Your minister, head of office or agency head approves. Heads of ministries, offices and agencies are approved by the Chief Minister.
for_specific_groups.Provincial governors and mayors of highl: The Chief Minister or a duly authorised representative approves.
for_specific_groups.Heads of office: You may deny an application where the absence would seriously hamper operations, must send the Office of the Chief Minister a copy of each approval within 10 days, and must keep a reporting system of applications, approvals and availments.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: All BARMM government offices: ministries, offices and agencies, Parliament, and local government units including barangays.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: Once the implementing rules are out — due within 60 days of approval, from the Office of the Chief Minister and the Office of the Speaker after consultation with the Civil Service Commission. The forms are set in those rules.
what_you_can_do: Check your aggregate service; 3 years across any Bangsamoro office or LGU counts
Apply well ahead, since a head of office may deny where operations would be seriously hampered
If denied, refile the next year; the act gives a refiled application priority
Keep records of your pilgrimage for the written report due within 30 days of your return
watch_out_for: Once in a lifetime, regardless of which office you work in when you apply.
Taking the leave and deliberately not performing the pilgrimage is an administrative offence under Civil Service Commission rules.
The act contains no appropriation; the leave is paid from existing salaries.
The approval block on the published copy reads “XXX”, and Parliament's acts index lists BAA 94 under the wrong title.

key_terms_explained.Pilgrimage: Visiting a place of recognised religious or spiritual importance in the employee's faith to perform acts of worship or a spiritual journey; for this act it may also include other meaningful spiritual or moral journeys recognised by the employee's traditions or conscience.
key_terms_explained.Pilgrimage Leave: A one-time paid leave of at most 22 working days to undertake pilgrimage.
key_terms_explained.LCE: Local chief executive — a governor or mayor.
key_terms_explained.Non-monetisation: Unused leave cannot be converted to cash.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Safar 02, 1448 / 16 July 2026. The published copy bears the Speaker's signature; the approval block reads “XXX”.

benefits.headline: Up to 22 paid working days for a pilgrimage, once in a career.

direct_benefits.benefit: Paid leave of at most 22 working days to perform a pilgrimage
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: BARMM officials and employees with 3 years of aggregate service
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Apply to your approving authority under Section 5, using the forms in the implementing rules

indirect_benefits: Priority for a refiled application after an operational denial
limitations: May be denied where it would seriously hamper operations.

for_citizens: If you take the leave: perform the pilgrimage, and file a written report with your approving authority within 30 days of returning to work.
If you are a head of office: copy approvals to the Office of the Chief Minister within 10 days and maintain a reporting system of applications, approvals and availments.

what_is_prohibited: Deliberately failing to perform the pilgrimage after taking the leave.

penalties.for_citizens: Administrative sanctions and penalties under Civil Service Commission rules for an employee who deliberately fails to perform the pilgrimage despite taking the leave. No fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own. Administrative matters fall under Civil Service Commission rules.

everyday_scenarios: A teacher with 4 years in a Bangsamoro ministry applies for leave to perform the Hajj. Her minister or head of office approves, sends the Office of the Chief Minister a copy within 10 days, and she files a written report within 30 days of returning.

A municipal employee's application is denied because his office is short-staffed during an audit. He refiles the next year, and the act gives his application priority, subject to the same operational test.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Short title: the “Pilgrimage Leave Act of 2026”.
Section 2 — Policy: a strong and highly motivated workforce; paid leave for pilgrimage supports spiritual and personal development, well-being and productivity.

Section 3 — Defines pilgrimage (a visit to a place of religious or spiritual importance in the employee's faith, and other meaningful spiritual or moral journeys recognised by the employee's traditions or conscience), Pilgrimage Leave (a one-time paid leave of at most 22 working days) and leave.

Section 4 — Officials and employees with an aggregate of 3 years of service in Bangsamoro ministries, offices, agencies or LGUs qualify. The leave may be taken once in a lifetime, whatever office the employee is in when applying.

Section 5 — Approval: the Chief Minister for heads of BMOAs; ministers and heads for their employees; the Speaker for Parliament's members and personnel; the Chief Minister or an authorised representative for governors and mayors of highly urbanised or independent component cities; governors for mayors of component cities and municipalities; local chief executives for LGU and barangay officials and employees. Approvals are copied to the OCM within 10 days. A head may deny an application that would seriously hamper operations; a refiled application the following year gets priority.
Section 6 — Heads of office maintain a reporting system of applications, approvals and availments for the OCM, to prevent duplication, abuse, misrepresentation and unauthorised availment.
Section 7 — A written report on the pilgrimage to the approving authority within 30 days of returning to work; forms in the IRR.
Section 8 — Deliberately failing to perform the pilgrimage despite taking the leave draws administrative sanctions under CSC rules.
Section 9 — Unused leave is not monetised.
Section 10 — IRR within 60 days of approval, issued jointly by the OCM and the Office of the Speaker after consultation with the CSC for BARMM, reviewed every 2 years.
Section 11 — Non-diminution of existing benefits under laws, decrees, executive orders or collective negotiation agreements.
Sections 12–14 — Repealing clause, separability, and effectivity 15 days after publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or a newspaper of regional circulation.

citizen_questions.q: Why does Parliament's acts index show a different title for BAA 94?
citizen_questions.a: The acts index repeats BAA 93's title under BAA 94. The enacted text published as BAA 94 is the Pilgrimage Leave Act of 2026, and the bills index traces BAA 94 to Bills 282 and 276.
